Where the number is computed: in a core ProjectSession method (pin_report, selection_status, cycle_time: 'one report, no surface computes it twice') versus a viz memo on state.simulation (cached_load_report, cached_cut_metrics) because the cut trace is held in viz state and not in session.simulation (rs_cam_core/tests/query_cycle_time_one_answer.rs header). A diagnostic that reads the trace must pick; the first needs the trace passed in as an argument.

Wire format: hand-built serde_json::json! (pin_report_json, mcp_get_tool_load_report) versus a serde derive on the core report type (ToolLoadReport via serde_json::to_value, generation.rs:~318). Both exist.

Diagnostic list versus new tool: adding a rule id in core diagnostics/ids.rs makes the value appear in get_toolpath_diagnostics and the GUI ribbon with an N4 parity test (tests/ribbon_and_mcp_diagnostic_ids_n4.rs), while the task asks for a new tool. Both patterns match 'a newly computed diagnostic value'.

Cheap snapshot read (cheap_read with McpReadKind, mcp_server.rs:194, five tools) versus plain send_request (get_tool_load_report). A cheap read also needs a McpReadSnapshot field and a pick arm (mcp_bridge.rs:20-70).

Where the GUI shows it: Inspector cut-metric card (ui CLAUDE.md, Metrics tab), Readiness panel limit rows (readiness_panel.rs), simulation diagnostics (sim_diagnostics.rs), or a verdict pill (components/pill.rs). Each has its own sentry set and none is named as the default for a new diagnostic.

Two folder CLAUDE.md files own overlapping pieces: app/CLAUDE.md for the tool and ui/CLAUDE.md or state/CLAUDE.md for the panel and memo. Neither tells you to update the other; the parity step is not owned by one file.
